# My AI Story {.center style="text-align: center;" background-image="2023-09-12 NIEHS Council//dtt_slide_header.jpg" background-size="contain" background-repeat="no-repeat" background-position="top"}

![ChatGPT Logo](2023-09-12\ NIEHS\ Council/ChatGPT_logo.svg){height=700px}

::: notes
I first used ChatGPT in December of last year. The first time that I tried it, I thought that the technology was neat, but I didn't see the full potential. Then in January and February, I watched a few YouTube videos that showed some of the abilities that ChatGPT had. It was then that I realized that this technology could be used to solve some of the problems that we were facing in our research.
:::

# Did I go overboard?

::: {.fragment}
![](2023-09-12\ NIEHS\ Council/raindrop_bookmark_count.png)
:::

::: {.fragment}
![](2023-09-12\ NIEHS\ Council/github_stars.png)

::: notes
So since the beginning of the year, I've completely immersed myself in the world of AI and machine learning. I've read hundreds of articles and watched dozens of videos. I've also spent a lot of time playing around with various AI technologies, including ChatGPT, ChemCrow, and others. I've also spent a lot of time thinking about how these technologies could be used to solve problems in environmental health sciences, especially in understanding GxE interactions.
:::

## Notes

-   Example can be to query ROBOKOP using natural language, then summarize the results

-   So the first is the fact that you can actually find something that's true. The second is now that you've found something that's true, you can hypothesize something, and that's something that you can test. And I think that's an important thing to get across both there's some tangible reality to what it is synthesizing we already know. And then it has a capacity to hypothesize the same at the same time, which would be great.

-   One of the questions in theory, you could prompt secondary secondary to generating the profile is a set of hypotheses around interspecies translation.

-   Meaning, what's the evolutionary conservation of the known targets of toxicological effect that would be challenging with certain chemicals?

-   Like furan, because it's just like scorched earth, but for other things like estradiol or something along those lines, there's there's a resource actually the DPA made that was really great that looked at the evolutionary conservation of the pocket space.
